subtitle: Tunable Modal Resonator
tagline: A playable modal instrument that turns any input into a tuned physical body, with eight resonant modes, zero latency, and tails up to 30 seconds.

body.lead: TB Resonator turns any input into a tuned physical object. Eight stable resonant modes give clicks, drums, noise, guitars, pads, or vocals a defined pitch, material, and memory.

body.p: `TUNE` sets the musical centre. `BODY` moves the material between harmonic and inharmonic structures. `TOUCH` changes how transients and sustained energy excite the object. `MEMORY` controls how long the modes ring, and `MIX` balances the transformation with the original. TB Resonator adds no latency, works in mono or stereo, and its tails can last up to 30 seconds.

ul: Eight resonant modes tuned from C1 to C7
BODY from SOFT through WOOD, STRING, and GLASS to METAL
TOUCH from STRIKE through PLUCK, NATURAL, and OPEN to DRIVE
12 factory presets in three groups, user presets, undo, and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Resonator 1.0.1 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is also version 1.0.1; small differences between platforms are possible.

ol: Insert TB Resonator on drums, a guitar, a pad, or a vocal. The defaults are `TUNE` C3, `TOUCH` 50%, `BODY` 50%, `MEMORY` 1.10 s, and `MIX` 35%.
Set `TUNE` {{2}} to the key of the song, or to a note that fits the chord.
Choose the material with `BODY` {{4}}: soft and woody to the left, glassy and metallic to the right.
Set how the input strikes the object with `TOUCH` {{3}}.
Set the ring length with `MEMORY` {{5}} and the blend with `MIX` {{6}}.

rows: C1 to C7 (MIDI 24 to 96) · C3 (130.8 Hz)
Chooses the fundamental note remembered by the resonator. The display shows the note and its frequency.
Moves from transient-only excitation to open, driven excitation. The readout names the range: STRIKE, PLUCK, NATURAL, OPEN, DRIVE.
Morphs spacing, brightness, and high-mode decay as one material, from harmonic to inharmonic. The readout names the range: SOFT, WOOD, STRING, GLASS, METAL.
Sets how long the resonant object remembers each excitation.
Blends the resonant object with the original signal at equal power.

body.p: TB Resonator also has a host Bypass parameter for comparing the dry and processed sound.

warn.text: Long MEMORY settings and strong low notes can build up level and low-frequency energy. Watch the output level and low end when you lengthen the ring.

body.p: Step through factory presets with the arrows; hold an arrow to browse continuously. Open the list to choose a factory preset or load a user preset. Save stores the current settings as a user preset. Undo and Redo step through recent parameter changes.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Tuned drums
recipes.use: Give a kick, tom, or percussion loop a pitch.
steps: Keep TOUCH low so only the hits excite the body.

recipes.title: Sympathetic strings
recipes.use: A ringing halo around guitar or piano.
steps: Tune to a note that sits in every chord of the section.

recipes.title: Glass voice
recipes.use: A tuned, glassy layer on vocals.
steps: Lower MIX if the words lose clarity.

recipes.title: Drone bed
recipes.use: A sustained, driven texture from any input.
steps: Watch the level as the tail builds up.

rows: The resonance clashes with the music.
Retune TUNE to the key, or to a note shared by the chords.
The sound gets boomy or too loud.
Shorten MEMORY, raise TUNE, or lower MIX.
Only hits ring, sustained parts do not.
Raise TOUCH toward OPEN or DRIVE.
Move BODY toward WOOD or STRING.
MIX is at 0%, or the host Bypass parameter is on.
